open_points.subject: answer_request request-bound measurement
open_points.text: After every request bound is checked on the texts as received, as the last step of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1). A text whose canonical form outgrows a bound it met as received is not refused here: the module that judges the value measures its canonical bytes, as start_run refuses a run input whose canonical bytes exceed the stored value ceiling.
open_points.other_text: Each JSON text the message carries as a string is measured on its own by canonical_bytes, so the message around it adds no depth to it. Request bounds, each counted as UTF-8 bytes of the field as received: implementation code within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_IMPLEMENTATION_CODE_BYTES_MAX constant; the json_text of a trial case input or expected output, of a flow constant and of a run input within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant; the decoded bytes of a trial case file within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every other string anywhere in the request within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant; a page_size given below 1 or above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_PAGE_SIZE_MAX constant; base64 text that does not decode; each a failure answered invalid_request (A16 rules 4 and 6).
open_points.question: Must a JSON-text bound be measured from its UTF-8 bytes as received, allowing a larger canonical form, or from canonical_bytes, which measures the canonical form and can reject it before the stated final canonical-replacement step?
